Method

Dossier format: offering and scope; disclosed delivery and operating model; buyer assessment and limits. Every qualifying supplier in the approved input is covered. First-party marketing is evidence of what is offered or reported, not an independently observed delivery. A named case is preserved at its actual attribution, task and date. A dossier with no named customer artifact established here is not evidence that the supplier has never delivered one. Unrecorded language, modality, security or commercial facets are unknown, not negative capabilities. Differentiation means a documented design or responsibility distinction, not a score for provider quality.

A.Team

Source-backed finding

A.Team — offering and scope. Its RL engineering offer includes graders, rubrics, harnesses and rollout infrastructure. A.Team lists golden trajectories, expert data and RLHF/RFT support within post-training pipeline work. A.Team offers senior engineers to build and validate training environments, tasks and evaluations.

Evidence: candidate.cohort5.a-team.graders-harnesses, candidate.cohort5.a-team.posttraining-pipelines, candidate.cohort5.a-team.rl-engineering-offer

Source-backed finding

A.Team — disclosed delivery and operating model. A.Team offers hourly, contract-to-hire, ongoing and advisory builder engagements. Its RL page says builders work within customer access controls, reviews and governance.

Evidence: candidate.cohort5.a-team.delivery-model, candidate.cohort5.a-team.security-perimeter

Source-backed finding

A.Team — source-specific boundaries. These are engagement models, not client prices, worker compensation amounts or evidence of completed named-artifact delivery. Provider disclosure; no security audit report, scope or project execution was independently inspected.

Evidence: candidate.cohort5.a-team.delivery-model, candidate.cohort5.a-team.graders-harnesses, candidate.cohort5.a-team.posttraining-pipelines, candidate.cohort5.a-team.rl-engineering-offer, candidate.cohort5.a-team.security-perimeter

Analysis

A.Team — buyer assessment and unknowns. The useful comparison is engineering accountability: request a concrete environment, grader or harness milestone and clarify whether the buyer is purchasing individual time or a warranted deliverable. Customer access controls should appear in the project specification. Builder engagement models alone do not establish delivered data quality, a fixed completion price or current specialist availability. Confidence is moderate for the disclosed scope and unestablished for independently measured operational performance. The assessment would change with independently accepted engineering milestones and access-control records.

Evidence: candidate.cohort5.a-team.delivery-model, candidate.cohort5.a-team.graders-harnesses, candidate.cohort5.a-team.posttraining-pipelines, candidate.cohort5.a-team.rl-engineering-offer, candidate.cohort5.a-team.security-perimeter

Source-backed finding

Abundant — offering and scope. Abundant lists coding, sciences, engineering, RSI, alignment and robotics as focus areas. Foundry offers to turn Fireworks customers’ own product data and workflows into RL environments. Abundant advertises creation of environments and datasets for reinforcement learning.

Evidence: candidate.cohort4.abundant_ai.advertised-domains, candidate.cohort4.abundant_ai.foundry-customer-offer, candidate.cohort4.abundant_ai.rl-data-environments

Source-backed finding

Abundant — disclosed delivery and operating model. Abundant says every Foundry task version receives human sign-off after automated and adversarial QA. Abundant says Foundry starts from customer product data including user sessions, tools and golden test cases. Abundant describes Oddish as tooling for trials, trace capture, scheduling and environment revision before human review.

Evidence: candidate.cohort4.abundant_ai.foundry-qa-signoff, candidate.cohort4.abundant_ai.foundry-task-inputs, repair.qualbinding.20261111.v1.candidate.cohort4.abundant_ai.oddish-validation-loop

Source-backed finding

Abundant — source-specific boundaries. Listed focus areas do not establish named customer work, linguistic coverage or worker headcount. The article separately describes baseline, adversarial and multi-agent stress tests; the execution of those checks was not independently audited.

Evidence: candidate.cohort4.abundant_ai.advertised-domains, candidate.cohort4.abundant_ai.foundry-customer-offer, candidate.cohort4.abundant_ai.foundry-qa-signoff, candidate.cohort4.abundant_ai.foundry-task-inputs, repair.qualbinding.20261111.v1.candidate.cohort4.abundant_ai.oddish-validation-loop, candidate.cohort4.abundant_ai.rl-data-environments

Analysis

Abundant — buyer assessment and unknowns. The differentiating disclosed workflow starts from customer product traces and golden cases and closes with task-version sign-off. A pilot should inspect trace permissions, reset behavior and the recorded transition from automated stress tests to human acceptance. A list of scientific and coding focus areas does not establish task coverage or operational throughput in each domain. Confidence is moderate for the disclosed scope and unestablished for independently measured operational performance. The assessment would change with trace-to-task lineage, reset tests and independent task-version sign-off.

AfterQuery

Source-backed finding

AfterQuery — offering and scope. AfterQuery offers human demonstrations across browser and desktop environments as computer-use trajectories. AfterQuery offers SFT prompt–response pairs and reasoning traces for complex tasks. AfterQuery offers expert-designed prompts and grading frameworks for reasoning and code generation.

Evidence: candidate.cohort4.afterquery.computer-use-demonstrations, candidate.cohort4.afterquery.expert-sft, candidate.cohort4.afterquery.rubric-reinforcement

Source-backed finding

AfterQuery — disclosed delivery and operating model. AfterQuery attributes office-task input for NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra to its own delivery account. The linked NVIDIA report was not independently retrieved; this does not establish GDPval authorship or a share of all training data. AfterQuery’s website privacy policy excludes personal-information processing performed as a processor or service provider for customers. AfterQuery’s terms place service fees in separate agreements or order forms.

Evidence: repair20261111.claim.current-reference217, candidate.cohort4.afterquery.processor-privacy-boundary, candidate.cohort4.afterquery.separate-service-pricing

Source-backed finding

AfterQuery — source-specific boundaries. Evidence is AfterQuery’s first-party delivery account, including its quoted NVIDIA-report passage; the linked NVIDIA PDF was not retrieved or independently read. It attributes office-task input, not GDPval authorship, all training data or model performance. The policy’s general security statement does not establish customer-processing contractual safeguards, certifications or specific worker protections.

Evidence: candidate.cohort4.afterquery.computer-use-demonstrations, candidate.cohort4.afterquery.expert-sft, repair20261111.claim.current-reference217, candidate.cohort4.afterquery.processor-privacy-boundary, candidate.cohort4.afterquery.rubric-reinforcement, candidate.cohort4.afterquery.separate-service-pricing

Analysis

AfterQuery — buyer assessment and unknowns. The buyer can distinguish demonstrations, prompt-response data and grading frameworks as separate outputs. The named office-task account is useful for requesting an artifact-specific sample, but its first-party attribution cannot be extended to all NVIDIA data or GDPval authorship. Obtain the customer-processing agreement and project order because the general website policy and terms leave those details elsewhere. Confidence is moderate for the disclosed scope and unestablished for independently measured operational performance. The assessment would change with customer-confirmed office-task provenance and independently scored trajectories.

Alegion / SanctifAI data services — source-specific boundaries. Provider business-structure disclosure; legal ownership and corporate registry have not been independently checked. Access-to-workforce language is not a current paid-active count or assignment total; the source’s large pool figure is not adopted.

Source-backed finding

Alinia AI — offering and scope. Alinia advertises adversarial evaluation against a customer’s policy red lines. Alinia offers policy judges trained on internal and external policies to check AI outputs.

Evidence: candidate.cohort5.alinia.adversarial-evaluation, candidate.cohort5.alinia.policy-judge-service

Source-backed finding

Alinia AI — disclosed delivery and operating model. Its engagement process compares judge decisions with customer experts on real data. Alinia describes each engagement as a forward deployed legal and engineering project inside the customer environment. The website privacy policy names Alinia AI, Inc. as data controller.

Evidence: candidate.cohort5.alinia.expert-validation, candidate.cohort5.alinia.forward-deployed-model, candidate.cohort5.alinia.privacy-entity

Source-backed finding

Alinia AI — source-specific boundaries. This describes a proposed validation stage; it is not independent evidence of accuracy, legal compliance or expert sign-off for a particular deployment. Website-controller identity does not prove equity ownership or recertify every historical alias. The policy’s website scope does not replace a customer processing agreement.

Evidence: candidate.cohort5.alinia.adversarial-evaluation, candidate.cohort5.alinia.expert-validation, candidate.cohort5.alinia.forward-deployed-model, candidate.cohort5.alinia.policy-judge-service, candidate.cohort5.alinia.privacy-entity

Analysis

Alinia AI — buyer assessment and unknowns. This is a policy-judge and integrated validation proposition. Require a customer-specific policy-to-test mapping and a blinded expert comparison before using judge outputs for operational decisions. The website controller identity is not a customer-data protection agreement, and an engagement description involving legal expertise is not a finding that a deployment complies with law. Confidence is moderate for the disclosed scope and unestablished for independently measured operational performance. The assessment would change with held-out expert policy judgments and complete false-accept/false-reject counts.

Appen

Source-backed finding

Appen — offering and scope. Appen offers repository tasks with verified patches, debugging traces, code preference pairs, and test-generation data. Appen offers expert alignment data, agentic workflows, multimodal data, physical-AI data, model evaluation, and research services.

Evidence: candidate.supplier.appen.coding, candidate.supplier.appen.offering

Source-backed finding

Appen — disclosed delivery and operating model. Appen describes project-level agreement metrics, continuous gold questions, and adjudication of disagreement. Appen’s FY2025 report describes a global crowd of more than one million experts and identifies CrowdGen as a platform. The 2025 annual report identifies Appen Limited as the parent entity. Appen says its model-evaluation work is run by teams separate from the training-data producers. Appen’s privacy statement permits service-provider processing and describes access controls and confidentiality duties for contractors. Appen markets consent records, licensing terms, and data lineage as delivery documentation. Appen reports FY2025 consolidated revenue from customer contracts of USD 230.774 million. Appen’s security page describes SOC 2 Type II attestation, a HIPAA-specific solution, and named secure-facility options. Appen reports FY2025 revenue of USD 127.874 million for Appen Global and USD 102.900 million for Appen China.

Evidence: candidate.supplier.appen.adjudication, candidate.supplier.appen.crowd-network, candidate.supplier.appen.entity, candidate.supplier.appen.evaluation-separation, candidate.supplier.appen.privacy-subcontractors, candidate.supplier.appen.provenance, candidate.supplier.appen.revenue-fy2025, repair20261111.claim.current-reference078, candidate.supplier.appen.segments-fy2025

Source-backed finding

Appen — source-specific boundaries. Crowd/network scope; no activity window, paid-contributor denominator, or paid assignment count is established. Report footnotes on geography/language need retention if those counts are used. Published privacy terms; the actual project subcontractor list, consent evidence, and contract-specific IP ownership were not inspected.

Evidence: candidate.supplier.appen.adjudication, candidate.supplier.appen.coding, candidate.supplier.appen.crowd-network, candidate.supplier.appen.entity, candidate.supplier.appen.evaluation-separation, candidate.supplier.appen.offering, candidate.supplier.appen.privacy-subcontractors, candidate.supplier.appen.provenance, candidate.supplier.appen.revenue-fy2025, repair20261111.claim.current-reference078, candidate.supplier.appen.segments-fy2025

Analysis

Appen — buyer assessment and unknowns. The breadth of disclosed modalities makes scope discipline central. A software-patch pilot and a physical-AI collection pilot should have separate acceptance units. Ask for evidence that the promised training/evaluation team separation and adjudication process operate on the proposed project. Group and geographic-segment revenue cannot identify the size or performance of expert generative-AI delivery. Confidence is moderate for the disclosed scope and unestablished for independently measured operational performance. The assessment would change with project-specific staffing, adjudication and matched accepted-unit results.

Centific

Source-backed finding

Centific — offering and scope. Centific’s OneForma page describes connecting model labs and enterprises with vetted contributors and domain experts for data, human feedback and model evaluation. Centific offers human preference signals suitable for training and refining reward models.

Evidence: candidate.cohort3.centific.oneforma-execution, candidate.cohort3.centific.preference-signals

Source-backed finding

Centific — disclosed delivery and operating model. OneForma describes conflict-resolution and consensus review workflows supported by automated labeling-error checks. Centific’s OneForma description states contributors are screened, identity-verified and continuously evaluated through quality checks. Centific describes trained evaluators ranking model outputs against nuanced criteria in its preference-optimization service. OneForma describes access-controlled environments and encrypted workflows for sensitive data.

Evidence: candidate.cohort3.centific.consensus-checks, candidate.cohort3.centific.contributor-screening, candidate.cohort3.centific.pairwise-raters, candidate.cohort3.centific.secure-facilities

Source-backed finding

Centific — source-specific boundaries. Provider process claim; no paid-active population or independent screening audit is inferred. Self-reported controls, not an independently inspected certification report.

Evidence: candidate.cohort3.centific.consensus-checks, candidate.cohort3.centific.contributor-screening, candidate.cohort3.centific.oneforma-execution, candidate.cohort3.centific.pairwise-raters, candidate.cohort3.centific.preference-signals, candidate.cohort3.centific.secure-facilities

Analysis

Centific — buyer assessment and unknowns. OneForma’s screening, consensus and automated checks should be evaluated as a sequence rather than one quality score.
